nodes.name: Cu substrate cleaning
nodes.procedure: Cu wire and cylinder were mechanically polished with sandpaper from 100 up to 1200 mesh. Besides, the following cleaning procedure was applied to all Cu electrodes before the coating depositions: degreasing in 10% NaOH solution, rinsing in Milli-Q water, pickling in 10% HCl solution, and, finally, rinsing again in Milli-Q water.

nodes.name: DES preparation
nodes.procedure: The DES preparation followed the procedure described in the literature [41]. The electroplating solutions prepared by the mixture of choline chloride (ChCl) (HOC2H4N(CH3)3Cl, Sigma-Aldrich, ≥98%) and urea U ((NH2)2CO, SigmaAldrich, ≥99%) in a molar ratio of 1:2 at 353.15K and containing different molar ratios of iron chloride (FeCl24H2O, Sigma-Aldrich ≥99%) and nickel chloride (NiCl26H2O, Sigma-Aldrich ≥99%).
nodes.source_text: The DES preparation followed the procedure described in the literature [41]...

nodes.name: Fe coating electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The Fe coating was electrodeposited on the Cu substrate from electroplating solution containing 0.5 mol L-1 FeCl2·4H2O in 1ChCl:2U under potentiostatic control for 30 min, at 353.15K and at -1.00 V vs. Ag/AgCl. All coatings were washed with water purified by the Milli-Q system to remove the solvent and then washed with isopropyl alcohol to remove the water adsorbed on the coating surfaces, and, finally, the sample was air-dried.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-rich coatings (Fe, Fe89Ni11, Fe69Ni31) show cracked morphology; Ni-rich coatings show spherical agglomerates and micronodules.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The top surface morphologies of the electrodeposited coatings are shown in Fig. 2(b-h). The examination of the images revealed that the Fe-rich coatings... are cracked... for electrodeposits containing a high percentage of Ni, the top surface examination exposed a change to spherical agglomerates structures...

Fig. 2a shows the chemical composition of the Fe_xNi_(1-x) electrodeposits obtained by EDS... Analysing Table 1, it can be concluded that the Fe content in the electrodeposited coatings was always lower than the concentration of Fe2+ ions...

nodes.characterization_summary: All coatings show Cu substrate fcc peaks at 2θ ~50° and 60° ({111},{200}). Peak broadening at 2θ ~53° indicates Fe-Ni alloy bcc phase overlap. Ni-rich coatings (Fe8Ni92, Ni) show fcc Ni peaks at 2θ ~49°, 52°, 61°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3 shows the XRD patterns achieved for Fe, Ni, and Fe_xNi_(1-x) coatings. In all patterns, it is possible to identify peaks with angle 2θ at about 50 and 60°, which were indexed to... Cu substrate... no peak referring to the body-centered cubic phase (bcc) related to α-Fe was detected... Ni-rich coatings... revealed peaks at 2θ around 49, 52, and 61°...

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe89Ni11: Bhf distribution max 34.6 T (bcc α-Fe-like); Fe69Ni31: 33.1 T; Fe47Ni53: 31.0 T; Fe28Ni72: 28.7 T (chemically disordered taenite phase). Fe89Ni11 and Fe69Ni31 show paramagnetic singlet (Fe in Cu fcc).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4(a-d) shows the room temperature Mössbauer spectra of coatings Fe89Ni11, Fe69Ni31, Fe47Ni53, and Fe28Ni72... the Mössbauer spectra was fitted by a Bhf distribution, with the highest probability of Bhf centered on 34.6 T... reduction of the hyperfine magnetic field... due to the formation of a new atomically disordered magnetic phase...

nodes.characterization_summary: All coatings show ferromagnetic behavior with low coercivity (soft magnetic): Fe 328 Oe, Fe89Ni11 292 Oe, Fe69Ni31 185 Oe, Fe47Ni53 126 Oe, Fe28Ni72 83 Oe, Fe8Ni92 92 Oe, Ni 125 Oe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The magnetic properties of the Fe, Ni, and Fe_xNi_(1-x) coatings were investigated... The coercivity of coatings Fe, Fe89Ni11, Fe69Ni31, Fe47Ni53, Fe28Ni72, Fe8Ni92, and Ni was around 328, 292, 185, 126, 83, 92, and 125 Oe, respectively. Such results suggested that the coatings were soft magnetic materials...

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) measured at non-Faradaic potentials to determine ECSA values: Fe 111.2 cm², Fe89Ni11 58.1 cm², Fe69Ni31 37.7 cm², Fe47Ni53 43.5 cm², Fe28Ni72 42.2 cm², Fe8Ni92 27.2 cm², Ni 21.3 cm² (Cs = 0.040 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemically active surface areas (ECSA) for all Fe, Ni and Fe_xNi_{1-x} electrocatalysts were determined from the electrochemical double-layer capacitance (C_dl) of each electrocatalytic coating using Eq. (1)... The results showed that the Fe and Fe_{89}Ni_{11} electrocatalysts exhibit the highest ECSA values among all the investigated materials with 111.2 and 58.1 cm², respectively.
